newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Trade in Ciba Speciality begins March 13.
newsitem.headline: Trade in Ciba Speciality begins March 13.

text.p: Bourse trading in the shares of Ciba Specialty Chemicals AG, a company that is being spun off from Novartis AG, is planned to begin on March 13, the company said.

In a statement issued ahead of a news conference, Ciba Specialty characterised the spin-off as one of the largest in the world and said it would result in a company with annual sales that exceeded 6.7 billion Swiss francs in 1996.
Shares of the new company, currently a 100-percent subsidiary of Novartis, will be offered to shareholders of Novartis in a one-for-one ratio at a subscription price of 10 francs.
The issue price of the new shares will be announced later.
On February 26 the two-week subscription period and trading in subscription rights will begin, the company said, adding further details of the spin-off would be announced February 18.

Between February 18 and March 11 the management of Ciba Speciality will be conducting road shows for potential investors where they also will arrange book building for the shares that will be offered to the general public.
Credit Suisse First Boston and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) are coordinating the transaction.
Ciba Specialty has been operating as an independent unit since January 1 and the company has now announced the members of its board of directors.

Two members of Ciba's management have already been proposed to the board: Rolf Meyer, former chief financial officer of Ciba-Geigy AG, is designated president of Ciba Specialty, and Hermann Vodicka, previously chief executive of Ciba-Geigy AG, is chief executive of Ciba Specialty Chemicals.
The other members of the board that will be proposed to the annual shareholders meeting are:
-- Erwin Heri, chief financial officer of Winterthur Insurance.
-- Gertrud Hoehler, advisors to several German companies such as Deutsche Bank, Mercedes and Volkswagen.
-- Jean-Marie Pierre Lehn, Nobel prize winner in chemistry in 1987.
-- Peter Littmann, chief executive of Hugo Boss AG.
-- Armin Meyer, member of the board of ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG.
-- Theodor Tschopp, chairman and chief executive of Alusuisse-Lonza AG.
